whatItIs.text: Dried and crushed (not ground) cayenne-type chillies, usually blended from up to four cultivars in the 30,000-50,000 Scoville range; the pizza-table standard.

historyNote.text: Chillies were harvested in Central and South America from about 7,500 BC; the crushed-flake form is credited to the Macedonian village of Bukovo — whose name (bukovo, bukovska piper) still labels the flakes across Southeast Europe — and Southern Italians carried the habit to America in the 19th century.

howToChoose.text: Buy in small quantities from high-turnover shelves — the flakes fade within about a year; a vivid red colour means decent heat remains.

storage.text: Keep in an airtight jar away from heat and light. The rulebook has the spice-shelf guidance.
storage.note: spice storage guidance lives in the food-safety rulebook

useItUp.text: Faded flakes still work toasted briefly in oil, or blitzed into chili crisp and hot sauces where other flavours carry them.

substitutions.note: same heat range, finer texture and even spread
much milder with smoke; colour without burn
